question: What is the primary purpose of Post-Abortion Care services in healthcare facilities?

options.B: Providing routine antenatal checkups for pregnant women
options.C: Screening communities for chronic infectious diseases
options.D: Treating complications from spontaneous or induced abortions

explanation: PAC is specifically structured to handle emergency medical and surgical complications resulting from pregnancy terminations or miscarriages. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h1)

question: Why does Post-Abortion Care extend beyond immediate clinical treatment?

options.A: To keep patients admitted in the ward for extended observation
options.B: To address the psychological and reproductive health needs of clients
options.C: To fulfill mandatory administrative reporting quotas for the ministry
options.D: To reduce the overall operational costs of the health facility

explanation: Clinical stabilization is only the first step; holistic care includes counseling, emotional support, and family planning integration. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h1)

question: How many core elements make up the complete Post-Abortion Care model?
explanation: The globally recognized PAC framework consists of five distinct, mutually reinforcing elements. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h2)

question: When should family planning counseling ideally occur during Post-Abortion Care?

options.A: After a mandatory six-week postpartum review clinic
options.B: During the initial emergency resuscitation phase
options.C: Before the client is discharged from the facility
options.D: Only when specifically requested by the patient's family

explanation: Providing contraception before discharge ensures the client is protected against rapid repeat unintended pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h2)

question: What is the main goal of conducting a community readiness assessment for PAC?

options.A: Determining the exact financial budget required for building wards
options.B: Understanding local beliefs and factors affecting service utilization
options.C: Selecting senior nursing staff for specialized overseas training
options.D: Procuring surgical instruments from international pharmaceutical vendors

explanation: Assessing the community helps identify cultural barriers and ensures that newly introduced services align with local realities and needs. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h3)

question: Who plays a key role in leading community sensitization campaigns to build trust in PAC?
explanation: Nurses act as frontline educators who bridge the gap between formal health institutions and the communities they serve. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h3)

question: Which instrument is commonly utilized for uterine evacuation during manual PAC procedures?
explanation: MVA kits are safe, highly effective tools used globally for uterine evacuation in the treatment of incomplete abortion. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h4)

question: Why is maintaining an adequate inventory of MVA kits and analgesics critical in PAC?

options.A: To comply with federal taxation laws for medical importation
options.B: To ensure the facility passes routine environmental sanitation checks
options.C: To reduce the overall duration of nursing shift handovers
options.D: To prevent dangerous clinical delays in managing hemorrhage and sepsis

explanation: Abortion complications can rapidly deteriorate into life-threatening emergencies, requiring immediate access to functional equipment and medicines. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h4)

question: What is the primary advantage of competency-based training over traditional lectures in PAC?

options.A: It focuses exclusively on administrative record keeping duties
options.B: It emphasizes hands-on practical skills and supervised clinical practice
options.C: It eliminates the need for any ongoing professional supervision
options.D: It reduces the total number of required training hours to zero

explanation: Competency-based learning ensures that nurses and doctors can perform clinical procedures safely and confidently on real patients. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h5)

question: Which skill is considered essential for clinical providers undergoing PAC capacity building?
explanation: Mastery of MVA is a core competency required for managing incomplete abortion safely in low-resource settings. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h5)

question: What is the immediate priority when managing a patient presenting with severe post-abortion hemorrhage?

options.A: Conducting a detailed family planning interview
options.D: Discharging the client home with oral analgesics

explanation: Resuscitation and hemodynamic stabilization always take precedence in any emergency medical or surgical complication. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h6)

question: When is the administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics specifically indicated in PAC cases?

options.A: Only after the client completes a full six-week postnatal check
options.B: When signs of pelvic infection or sepsis are present
options.C: Whenever the client requests immediate hormonal contraception
options.D: As a routine prophylactic for every client seeking family planning

explanation: Infection control requires targeted or broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy to manage sepsis arising from septic abortions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h6)

question: What makes post-abortion family planning counseling effective for clients?

options.A: Restricting choices to oral contraceptive pills alone
options.B: Being voluntary, confidential, and tailored to individual life plans
options.C: Requiring spousal consent before any contraceptive is dispensed
options.D: Focusing exclusively on permanent surgical sterilization options

explanation: Client-centered counseling respects patient autonomy and dramatically improves long-term contraceptive continuation rates. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core principle of good PAC counseling?

options.A: Coercing the client into accepting a specific method
options.B: Maintaining strict medical confidentiality at all times
options.C: Providing accurate information on various contraceptives
options.D: Respecting the personal autonomy of the patient

explanation: PAC counseling must never be coercive; clients retain the absolute right to accept or decline any family planning method. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h7)

question: How do clinical audits and near-miss reviews contribute to PAC quality improvement?

options.A: By identifying systemic gaps and learning from clinical errors
options.B: By determining individual disciplinary suspensions for staff members
options.C: By calculating the exact hospital profit margins each month
options.D: By increasing the paperwork burden for frontline nurses

explanation: Analyzing near-misses helps facilities fix operational bottlenecks and prevent future adverse clinical outcomes. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h8)

question: What type of environment is necessary for effective incident reporting in quality improvement?
explanation: Staff are more likely to report errors and near-misses honestly when the institutional culture focuses on learning rather than punishment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h8)
